name: Cetirizine
route_note: Oral tablet or syrup once daily; eye drops for allergic conjunctivitis; IV formulation (US) for acute urticaria
owner: generic (many); Zyrtec brand: Kenvue (US) and others

discovery.note: The carboxylic-acid metabolite of the first-generation antihistamine hydroxyzine, with less penetration into the brain. Year of first patent (1983), per Wikipedia.

tagline: Widely used once-daily non-sedating antihistamine for hay fever and hives
summary: Cetirizine is a second-generation H1 antihistamine derived from hydroxyzine. Taken once daily, it relieves allergic rhinitis and urticaria with less sedation than older antihistamines, though somewhat more than loratadine or fexofenadine.
mechanism: Cetirizine is a selective inverse agonist at peripheral histamine H1 receptors, stabilising the receptor in its inactive state and preventing histamine-induced vasodilation, vascular leak, itch and sneezing.
Its zwitterionic structure and P-glycoprotein efflux limit penetration into the central nervous system. It also has some anti-inflammatory effects, such as reduced eosinophil migration.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Zyrtec (marketed with Pfizer) as a prescription drug.

history.title: Levocetirizine
history.detail: The active R-enantiomer levocetirizine (Xyzal) is launched in Europe.

history.title: OTC in the US
history.detail: Zyrtec switches to over-the-counter status in the US.

history.title: IV cetirizine
history.detail: FDA approves Quzyttir, an intravenous cetirizine injection for acute urticaria.

facts: Cetirizine is the major active metabolite of hydroxyzine.
Because it is cleared by the kidneys, cetirizine doses are reduced in renal impairment.
